business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Sales of Musical Instruments and Studio Audio Gear

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Switzerland-United States Double Taxation Agreement (signed 1996, amended 2011)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA, SR 955.0) of 10 October 1997, as amended; Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220), Arts. 620-763 (Aktiengesellschaft); Commercial Register Ordinance (SR 221.411); FINMA Circular 2024/01 on anti-money-laundering; Swiss UBO transparency obligations arising from Art. 4 AMLA and financial intermediary client due diligence rules, with shareholder register requirements under Art. 697j OR.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and signed Articles of Association (Statuten / Statuts)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss public notary of the canton of registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic Swiss notarization; no apostille required for filing with the Swiss Commercial Register (apostille needed only if the document is later used abroad)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank confirmation of paid-up registered share capital (minimum CHF 50,000 for AG) and blocked account verification (Sperrkonto)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss bank where incorporation capital is deposited
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Direct written confirmation to the notary and Commercial Register; no apostille required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized or certified UBO declaration (economic beneficial owner) and first shareholder register entry (Art. 697j OR)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ultimate beneficial owner(s) before a Swiss public notary or foreign notary with legalization
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for signatories from Hague member states; Consular Legalization by the Swiss representation for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified corporate extracts, certificates of good standing, and passport copies of foreign corporate shareholders and UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry and passport authorities of each shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for Hague member states; Consular Legalization by the Swiss Embassy/Consulate for non-Hague jurisdictions

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the consolidated Swiss sanctions lists published by SECO (State Secretariat for Economic Affairs), the UN Security Council sanctions and travel-ban list, EU restrictive measures (adopted autonomously by Switzerland), OFAC SDN/Sectoral Sanctions lists for USD-denominated transactions and Fintech/Payment processor counterparties, and PEP databases using the Swiss definition under AMLA and FINMA Circular 2024/01. Enhanced due diligence and plausible source-of-wealth documentation are required for foreign PEPs, particularly those holding Swiss bank accounts or payment-processing accounts with Stripe or PayPal.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix - Official Central Business Name Index and Commercial Register Portal (zefix.ch); name clearance is filed through the cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) competent for the registered office.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be capable of being represented in one of the Swiss national languages (German, French, Italian, or Romansh). Non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin script. An Aktiengesellschaft must include the statutory suffix 'Aktiengesellschaft' or the abbreviation 'AG' in German, 'Société Anonyme'/'SA' in French, or 'Società Anonima'/'SA' in Italian. The name must comply with Art. 950 OR, must state or describe the purpose, must not be misleading, must not infringe third-party rights, and must not contravene public order or morality.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: An advance name clearance (Vorbescheid) issued by the cantonal Commercial Register Office is valid for 90 days and cannot be formally extended; upon expiry, a new application for preliminary name examination must be submitted. If the name is rejected, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Cantonal Commercial Register Supervisory Authority (kantonale Handelsregisteraufsichtsbehörde) within 30 days of receipt of the rejection decision. If the supervisory authority upholds the rejection, an appeal may be lodged with the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht) in St. Gallen. Where rejection is based on a third-party trademark or copyright conflict, the applicant should seek IP-litigation remedies before the Federal Patent Court or civil courts.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure correspondence-only virtual office is NOT permitted as the registered seat of a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft. The AG must have a genuine physical registered office in a Swiss municipality where the management actually administers the company (Art. 62 para. 1 and Art. 627 OR). A serviced office or business suite may qualify only if it provides a physical desk/room under a local service contract and the company maintains actual administrative presence; the Commercial Register will reject mail-dropping or letterbox-only arrangements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - estimated below 5% per year for a low-risk online musical-instruments and audio-gear retailer. Swiss commercial register authorities rarely conduct unannounced on-site inspections, but such inspections can be triggered by lender or payment-processor complaints, criminal information, or company insolvency indications.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Advance name clearance ruling (Vorbescheid) - one name examination fee
Notarization of Articles of Association, incorporation resolutions, and UBO declarations
Share capital verification and blocked account confirmation coordination
Certified translation of foreign UBO and corporate shareholder documents into German/French/Italian
Hague apostille and/or consular legalization of foreign UBO and shareholder documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authorities of document source countries and Swiss consular post

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, SR 220), Articles 620–625 (formation of the stock corporation), 621 (minimum nominal capital), 626–629 (content of the Articles of Incorporation and mandatory capital contributions), 640 (registration in the Commercial Register), and 716b (non-transferable powers of the Board of Directors).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce du canton), coordinated centrally via the Zefix business index and supervised by the Swiss Federal Commercial Register Office within the Federal Office of Justice (Bundesamt für Justiz).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of an Aktiengesellschaft (Anmeldung zur Eintragung einer Aktiengesellschaft) submitted through the eGRIS portal together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation (Statuten) and the public deed of formation (Errichtungsurkunde).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The AG requires a minimum nominal share capital of CHF 100,000. At formation, at least 20% (i.e., CHF 20,000) of the nominal capital must be fully paid up in cash. The paid-up funds must be deposited with a FINMA-regulated Swiss bank in a blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto) that remains frozen until the Commercial Register confirms the registration, after which the capital is released to the company's free disposal.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: UNANIMOUS WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] AG. The undersigned sole director, acting pursuant to Articles 620 et seq. and 716b of the Swiss Code of Obligations, resolves: (1) Share subscription of CHF 100,000 is confirmed, with CHF 20,000 paid into a blocked bank account in accordance with the mandatory capital payment rules. (2) The registered office at the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation is adopted. (3) The appointed director and authorized signatories with specimen signatures are ratified and instructed to complete commercial register filings and open the operational bank account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal public notary (Öffentliches Notariat / Étude de notaire)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Swiss notary to draft or review the Articles of Incorporation, including the corporate purpose limited to online retail of musical instruments and studio audio gear, the CHF 100,000 share capital, share classes, registered office address, and board composition. Perform a Zefix pre-check of the proposed company name to ensure uniqueness and legal admissibility. The notary authenticates the deed of formation, verifies founder identities and signatures, and issues the notarial deed recording the formation decision and the initial appointments.
required_dossiers: Passport or Swiss identity card of each founder
Written consent of each initial director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected by Zefix for conflict or misleading characteristics, file an amended name election with the notary. If the cantonal office considers the corporate purpose insufficiently precise, redraft the object clause to expressly cover 'online sale and distribution of musical instruments and audio equipment' before authentication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Paid-Up Capital in a Blocked Escrow Account (Sperrkonto)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss FINMA-regulated bank (cantonal bank, private bank, or licensed commercial bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account (Sperrkonto) in the name of the company to be formed. Deposit at least CHF 20,000, representing 20% of the CHF 100,000 minimum nominal capital, from the founders' or subscribers' funds. The bank issues a blocked-capital attestation confirming the deposit and stating that the account remains blocked until the Commercial Register registers the company, in line with Articles 628–629 of the Code of Obligations.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the Articles of Incorporation
Founder identification and beneficial owner declaration (Form A)
AML client risk profile and source-of-funds statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank escalates KYC or sanctions screening, supply the notarial deed and full source-of-funds documentation immediately. If the bank cannot issue a proper Swiss-law Sperrkonto attestation, select another FINMA-regulated bank and obtain a replacement attestation prior to the Commercial Register filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File for Entry in the Commercial Register (Handelsregistereintrag)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce) via eGRIS, published through Zefix
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the formal application for registration of the Aktiengesellschaft, including the notarized formation deed, the certified Articles of Incorporation, the bank blocked-capital attestation, the beneficial owner own-declaration, and the signed specimen signature cards of the directors and authorized signatories. Upon approval, the Commercial Register issues the certified excerpt (Handelsregisterauszug), enters the company into the register, and publishes the formation in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt).
required_dossiers: Blocked capital attestation from the depositary bank (Sperrkonto)
Beneficial owner declaration (form for the registration of beneficial interests)
Debt enforcement certificate (Betreibungsregisterauszug / Poursuites certificate) for authorized signatories
Director identification documents and specimen signature cards
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a deficiency notice, cure the deficiency within the allowed statutory period (typically 10 days) by resubmitting the corrected form or supplementary documents. If a beneficial-owner declaration is incomplete, file an amended declaration. If the statutory deadline cannot be met, formally apply for an extension with the cantonal Commercial Register Office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Secure UID, Cantonal Tax Registration, and VAT Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV / FTA / AFC) and the competent Cantonal Tax Administration (Kantonales Steueramt)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon publication of the registration, the company is automatically allocated a Swiss business identifier (UID). Verify the UID issuance via the Zefix/UID portal and complete the cantonal registration for corporate income tax and capital tax at the registered office's canton. Mandatorily register for VAT if annual worldwide taxable turnover is expected to exceed CHF 100,000, then submit the VAT registration through the ESTV portal for a VAT number valid for e-commerce sales of musical instruments and audio equipment.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation and notarial deed
Projected turnover forecast and place-of-business information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the UID is not automatically issued, apply directly to the ESTV with the registered excerpt. If VAT registration is delayed, the company may issue compliant invoices using the 'CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx' UID prefix once verified. If the cantonal tax office disputes the allocation, file a reassignment request through the cantonal tax commission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Operational Bank Accounts and Activate Payment Rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss commercial bank and third-party payment processors (Stripe and PayPal), with merchant verification by the relevant acquiring institutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the operating corporate bank account in the name of the registered AG (no longer blocked), and if required open a separate deposit account for cantonal collection of VAT and social deductions. Complete the Stripe and PayPal merchant onboarding under the Swiss legal entity, supplying the certified excerpt, UID number, and bank attestation. Connect the payment rails to the e-commerce platform and confirm the settlement currency settings with the bank.
required_dossiers: Director identity documents and specimen signature cards
Payment processor KYB questionnaire and website URL
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the payment processor requires additional business verification, resubmit the certified excerpt and a bank reference letter. If the bank delays the account opening, escalate through the designated relationship manager and provide the commercial register confirmation. If Stripe or PayPal reject the merchant application, submit the updated KYB documents to the processor's dedicated merchant support team before reapplying.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no sectoral industrial licensing board is involved because the activity is limited to non-hazardous online retail of musical instruments and studio audio gear, with no manufacturing or production facility in Switzerland.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required — the activity is conducted as an ordinary commercial business under the Swiss Code of Obligations; no manufacturing, production, or physical operating permit is mandated by the Confederation or the cantons.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU / FOEN / OFEV) with the cantonal environmental agency at the registered office address
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — pure online retail operations are outside the scope of Annex 1 of the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV / OEIE); no full EIA or registration is triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC, or stationary-source emission thresholds apply to the commercial activity. The company must only observe general waste-management duties under the Federal Act on the Protection of the Environment (Umweltschutzgesetz, USG), including proper packaging waste disposal and, where relevant, the take-back obligations for batteries and electronic components under the Swiss Ordinance on the Return, Take-Back and Disposal of Electrical and Electronic Equipment (ORDEE / VREG).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No specialized fire-safety or civil-defense permit is required for e-commerce and low-density warehouse operations. The company must satisfy cantonal fire-prevention requirements for its office/storage premises (smoke detectors, escape routes, portable extinguishers) and comply with SECO workplace safety and health guidelines, including SUVA accident-prevention rules for office and logistics staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC), tax portal: https://www.estv.admin.ch; VAT and UID e-services: https://www.e-service.estv.admin.ch
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity without a Swiss seat or permanent establishment must register with the ESTV for Swiss VAT if it makes taxable supplies in Switzerland and its annual worldwide Swiss-taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000. Procedure: submit the official VAT registration form (Formular 100 / Formulaire 100) via e-service or post, attach proof of incorporation (company extract/charter), evidence of Swiss business nexus (supply source, import/export customs records, local warehouse or agent), and appoint a Swiss tax representative if the entity has no residence in Switzerland or reciprocal recognition. Upon approval, ESTV issues the Swiss VAT identification number (MWST/TVA/IVA UID number, in practice UID-CH-XXXX-XXX-X). The UID also serves for VAT identification; TIN for direct tax matters is generally the same UID number. Registration is effective from the date of taxable activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Switzerland does not operate a US-style check-the-box election. For Swiss VAT, entities may elect voluntary VAT registration despite falling below the CHF 100,000 threshold; may elect VAT grouping (Art. 67 VAT Act) for economically integrated Swiss entities; and may apply to use the excess-input-tax method or simplified accounting methods under Art. 37 VAT Act. For direct federal, cantonal and communal taxes, the Aktiengesellschaft is taxed at entity level; no pass-through election is available. Hybrid mismatch elections are not generally recognized absent permanent establishment substance; certain group relief/notional interest deduction mechanisms do not apply in Switzerland except within cantonal tax conditions. Charitable non-profit entities may apply for tax-exempt status under Art. 56 lit. g LIFD.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Swiss VAT / MWST / TVA / IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual worldwide turnover from taxable supplies triggering mandatory Swiss VAT registration (Art. 110 VAT Act; voluntary registration permitted for lower turnover). Special low-rate regime applies to accommodation at 3.8% and reduced rate of 2.6% for necessities, publications, and certain cultural services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland has no mandatory real-time national fiscal clearance, API-driven e-invoicing clearance, or digital stamping obligation. Electronic invoices are permitted if they satisfy Art. 26a VAT Act content requirements; Swiss QR-bills, eBill, PEPPOL-style XML, and EDI are accepted. Invoices must be archived for 10 years in a format that allows electronic readability and presentation to ESTV upon request. There is no government pre-clearance of invoices; fiscal audit is ex post. Marketplaces or payment rails such as Stripe/PayPal do not replace VAT invoicing; the Swiss supplier remains responsible for proper invoicing, VAT collection, and export substantiation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Swiss VAT zero-rating for exports of goods applies where the goods are delivered to a destination outside Switzerland and are transported out of Switzerland by the supplier or an authorized third party; the supply must be evidenced by a customs export declaration or equivalent export document (Art. 23 VAT Act; Art. 52 VAT Ordinance). Services are zero-rated when the recipient is located abroad or the effective place of use/enjoyment lies abroad, including services rendered for or to a foreign business; proof of foreign receipt and business use is required. For online sales of musical instruments and studio audio gear, cross-border shipments must be supported by shipping documents (postal/air waybill), customs declarations, and payment records demonstrating foreign delivery. Input VAT incurred on purchases underlying exports is fully creditable against output VAT or refundable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss Customs Export Declaration (Zollanmeldung / déclaration en douane)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill / Postal Consignment Document
Delivery Note / Proof of Physical Removal from Switzerland
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT/Stripe/PayPal payment settlement evidence
Swiss VAT UID number and, if available, buyer VAT ID for business-to-business proof
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ESTV can retrospectively audit export zero-rating, require production of all evidence, and, if substantiation is incomplete, reclassify the supply as domestic taxable at 8.1%, assessing understated VAT plus default interest. Intentional VAT evasion carries administrative fines, generally up to the amount of tax evaded (Art. 105 VAT Act), and contravention fines up to CHF 10,000 (Art. 104 VAT Act). Fraudulent or false export declarations may trigger criminal proceedings and clawback of any refunded input VAT. The assessment/limitation period is generally 10 years for deliberate evasion; taxpayers bear an affirmative retention duty to preserve export evidence for 10 years. Penalties and interest accrue from the due date of the tax return; retrospective adjustment also applies to input VAT credits associated with disallowed zero-rating.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) / Schweizerische Nationalbank, with prudential supervision of banks exercised by the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) under the Federal Act on the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMASA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Swiss franc (CHF) is fully convertible. Switzerland imposes no exchange controls on either capital-account or current-account transactions under the Federal Act on Currency and Means of Payment (Currency Act), the Federal Act on the Swiss National Bank, and the Foreign Exchange Ordinance. Inbound capital contributions, outbound profit remittances, dividends, interest, royalties, loan repayments, and trade settlement payments are all free of SNB authorization requirements. The only material friction is the statutory 35% Swiss withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on dividend distributions and certain interest payments; the effective burden is typically reduced to 0-15% via double taxation treaties using Swiss Forms 822/823 relief-at-source or refund procedures. FATCA and the Swiss-AEOI disclosure regime require transparency but do not restrict convertibility. There is no requirement to obtain a capital-export license and no residual limitation on repatriating proceeds of online retail sales.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion obligations exist under Swiss law. Export receipts arising from the ISIC-4791 online retail of musical instruments and audio equipment may be held indefinitely in any convertible currency, retained in offshore accounts, or converted to CHF at the entity's discretion. There is no prescribed repatriation timeline and no minimum conversion ratio. Only statistical balance-of-payments reporting to the SNB applies when cumulative cross-border flows exceed defined reporting thresholds (customarily CHF 10 million), and even then the filing is informational rather than a currency-control measure.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Sperrkonto) / Multi-currency Operational Treasury Account (CHF, EUR, USD, GBP)
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account with SEPA and FX desk
Operational Multi-currency Account (CHF/EUR/USD) for e-commerce settlement
Operational Account for daily treasury and supplier payables
Operational Account optimized for Stripe and PayPal payout corridors
Operational Account with SEPA/SIC rails and retail card settlement

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM for ancillary treasury functions; LOW for primary corporate banking. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise Business, Revolut Business, Payoneer, and Airwallex can lawfully be used by a Swiss AG for FX conversions, foreign-supplier disbursements, and receiving e-commerce aggregations from Stripe and PayPal in EUR, USD, GBP, or CNY. However, EMIs cannot serve as the exclusive banking backbone because: (i) they lack direct access to the Swiss SIC/SIC5 CHF clearing rail, making Swiss payroll, AHV social-security contributions, and Swiss VAT (MWST) payments impracticable; (ii) FINMA Circular 2016/07 and the Anti-Money Laundering Act require any institution holding client funds with Swiss nexus to be licensed as a Swiss financial intermediary, so an unauthorized EMI cannot legally provide inward payment collection from Swiss card acquirers on behalf of the AG; and (iii) the notary's capital confirmation for the statutory CHF 100,000 minimum capital (at least CHF 50,000 paid in) must be issued by a Swiss bank regulated under the Federal Banking Act, not by an EMI. The optimal blueprint is therefore an anchor relationship with a Swiss commercial bank backed by supplementary EMI accounts for currency corridors only.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person presence is the prevailing industry standard for a newly incorporated Swiss AG whose beneficial owners are foreign nationals. FINMA's video-identification regime (permissible under FINMA Circular 2016/07) is in practice accepted sparingly for corporate clients with cross-border e-commerce exposure and non-resident UBOs; tier-1 institutions (UBS, ZKB, BCV) normally require a physical interview with at least one signatory director at the bank's premises, typically in Zurich, Zug, Geneva, or Lugano. Remote onboarding is feasible at PostFinance, Migros Bank, or selective cantonal banks if all shareholders are Swiss tax residents and an electronic ID is used, but foreign-resident directors should expect a mandatory in-person or notarized-consulate verification. Directors unable to travel may appoint a Swiss fiduciary or holder of a power of attorney, but the ultimate beneficial owner must still undergo identification through certified passport copies, apostilled corporate extracts, and sworn source-of-wealth statements. For the capital escrow step specifically, the safest operational plan is to book a physical KYC appointment before commercial go-live to avoid payment-rail delays.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner resident in or connected to a sanctioned, high-risk, or tax-haven jurisdiction (e.g., Russia, Belarus, Iran, Panama, BVI, UAE non-free-zone entities) within the UBO chain of the Swiss AG.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled certificate of incorporation and current registry extracts of any holding entity; notarially certified passports of all shareholders; complete source-of-funds documentation for the CHF 100,000 capital injection (bank statements covering at least six months, sale-and-purchase agreement, inheritance deed, or gift declaration); prior three years of personal tax returns or a sworn net-wealth statement; FATCA/GIIN registration confirmation from the source bank; a clean sanctions-screening report from an independent KYC vendor; and a sworn declaration that funds are not connected to corruption, organised crime, or tax evasion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained lump-sum capital contribution in a single wire exceeding the plausible start-up revenue profile of an online musical-instrument retailer.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarially attested business plan and a 24-month cash-flow projection; executed supplier framework agreements and wholesale purchase orders for instruments and studio audio gear; signed or historical platform statements from Stripe and PayPal showing projected settlement volumes; a CFO or fiduciary letter explaining working-capital deployment; and lease or fulfillment-center agreements substantiating inventory prepayments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Letter-box substance concern: Swiss AG registered at a virtual office with no local employees, foreign management, and no physical or logistical footprint in Switzerland.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial lease or serviced-office agreement in Canton Zug or Zurich; a Swiss payroll mandate for at least one employee or an outsourcing contract with a licensed Swiss professional employer organization; Swiss VAT (MWST) registration certificate for e-commerce retail; a third-party Swiss fulfillment or bonded-warehouse agreement; board minutes documenting meetings held in Switzerland; and an economic-substance memorandum describing the decision-making and logistics chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disproportionate projected turnover from Stripe and PayPal aggregators relative to registered share capital and Swiss operational substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant agreements and MID (merchant ID) confirmations from Stripe and PayPal; historical or benchmark payout reports for comparable European sellers; order-level transaction samples with average ticket values; audited supplier invoices and drop-ship agreements; a board-approved treasury policy; and a written confirmation that customer funds are never held in the corporate treasury account in a fiduciary or client-money capacity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: US-person UBO or significant US-sourced digital sales triggering FATCA Chapter 4 withholding and Swiss-US QI-reporting exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed IRS Form W-9 for any US-curated beneficial owner or W-8BEN-E for the entity; Swiss Form 823 (relief at source) or Form 822 (refund); a FATCA GIIN registration number; a representation that the AG has no US trade-or-business activity; evidence of consent under the Swiss-US IGA for automatic exchange of information; and a distribution policy confirming no US-sourced payments will be made without proper reporting.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for the statutory CHF 100,000 initial capital: the shareholder wires at least CHF 50,000 into a notarial escrow account (Sperrkonto) held at a Swiss banking counterparty, using SWIFT MT103 from the source bank with Remittance Information (field 70) reading 'Kapitalerhoehung / Gesellschaft CH_AG' plus the notary engagement reference. The internationally preferred purpose-classification is ISO 20022 Purpose Code INTC (intra-company/capital infusion) or the narrative 'equity contribution' where free-text is permitted. No SNB approval is required. Banks should be given one business day's notice to effect a spot CHF/USD or CHF/EUR conversion before value date so that the credit lands in CHF to meet the paid-in-capital threshold. The notary relies on a bank confirmation letter (Kontobestätigung) issued to the company; after public notarization of the deed of incorporation and commercial-registry entry, the escrow block is lifted and funds are moved to the operational treasury account via SIC5 internal transfer. For inbound transfers above CHF 1 million, SNB payment-statistics declarations attach, but no license or regulatory consent is needed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlement and treasury outflows of an ISIC-4791 online retailer: (1) SWIFT MT103 (plain or cover method) for supplier invoices in USD, EUR, CNY, and JPY through the Swiss bank's correspondent network, using SEPA purpose codes where applicable (e.g., SUPP for supplier payments, TRAD for trade transactions, TREA for treasury transfers); (2) SEPA Credit Transfer for EU suppliers and for EUR payouts received from Stripe and PayPal Europe onto a Swiss CH IBAN active in the SEPA scheme; (3) Commercial Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700 series, UCP600) for high-value bulk imports of musical instruments and audio hardware, with MT754 advice of payment for post-negotiation settlement; (4) SWIFT gpi (Global Payments Innovation) tracking appended to wire transfers to provide end-to-end beneficiary confirmation; and (5) SWIFT MT400 documentary collections as a low-cost alternative to LCs for reliable counterparties. For CHF-denominated domestic payments, SIC5 real-time gross settlement is mandatory; for international CHF same-day transfers, the SWIFT rail routed through the SNB's settlement system is used. Outbound sweeps to Wise or other EMIs are executed as ordinary MT103 or SEPA transfers with the reference 'Treasury concentration to EMI overseas account'.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright FX forwards (vanilla forwards) in CHF/USD, CHF/EUR, CHF/GBP, and CHF/CNY with tenors from one week to twelve months, tradable under a bank's Simple FX Forward agreement without a full ISDA master for notionals below USD 1 million equivalent.

FX swaps (spot/forward and forward/forward combinations) used to convert USD or EUR receivables into CHF while retaining offshore liquidity, recognised as derivatives subject to FINMA market-risk Circular 2008/02 and reported per Swiss ordinances on derivative transparency.
Rolling spot deferred contracts and window forwards permitting flexible execution dates aligned with unsettled Stripe and PayPal settlement flows.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on exotic Asian and Latin American currencies such as offshore CNY, INR, and BRL, executed via the Swiss bank's global trading desk under an ISDA 2010 Swiss-law Annex; deliverable CHF crosses are preferred given the currency's full convertibility.

Short-dated OTC European-style FX options for fixed future supplier payments, permissible for a professional corporate client under the Financial Services Act (FinSA) hedging exemptions and not subject to prospectus requirements.

Cross-currency swaps (CCS/CRS) for long-term working-capital facilities denominated in foreign currency, collateralised under a Credit Support Annex and centrally cleared where the notional exceeds clearing thresholds required by Swiss and G20 clearing mandates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Combined federal and cantonal corporate income tax return with annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent cantonal tax administration and Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA); not filed with the Commercial Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the close of the financial year; for a calendar-year AG, normally by 30 June of the following year unless an extension is granted by the canton
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest on assessed taxes, procedural late-filing fines, tax evasion penalties, and enforced collection through Swiss debt collection and potential insolvency. Switzerland does not have an automatic administrative strike-off for late tax returns, but continuing untraceability or invalid organization may lead to court-ordered dissolution under Art. 731b CO.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA), VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of the VAT accounting period; the standard period is generally the calendar year unless the FTA has prescribed quarterly or semi-annual settlement periods
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: VAT default interest, late-filing penalties, and a penalty of up to 25% of the tax evaded in willful or grossly negligent cases; repeated failures can trigger enforced collection and bankruptcy proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual AHV/IV/EO employer wage declaration and employee salary statements (Lohnausweis) if the company has employees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss compensation office (AHV-Ausgleichskasse) responsible for the registered seat
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 January following the wage year for salary statements; employer social-insurance contribution statements must be delivered according to the contribution settlement periods prescribed by the compensation office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines, default interest on unpaid AHV/IV/EO contributions, priority collection of employer social-security contributions, and potential director liability for unlawfully withheld employee contributions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting, including approval of the financial statements and registration of any resulting changes to directors or auditors in the Commercial Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders and board of directors; Commercial Register (Handelsregister) only receives filings when board, auditor, or organizational data changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual general meeting must be held within six months after the balance-sheet date; any required Commercial Register filing must be made within 14 days of the relevant resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the AGM allows shareholders or creditors to petition the court to convene it; directors may be held liable for damages. Failure to register mandatory changes can result in Commercial Register fines, and an unsolved organizational defect may ultimately lead to judicial dissolution under Art. 731b CO.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An ordinary statutory audit is compulsory if the AG exceeds any two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total CHF 20 million, turnover CHF 40 million, or 250 full-time equivalent employees on annual average; a public company always requires an ordinary audit. An AG below these thresholds must have a limited statutory review unless all shareholders unanimously resolve to dispense with the audit and the company has an average of not more than 10 full-time employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Legal minimum annual accounts prepared under the Swiss Code of Obligations (Swiss GAAP OR); Swiss GAAP FER or IFRS may be adopted voluntarily for true-and-fair presentation and is accepted by Swiss tax authorities with reconciliation to statutory taxable income.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss law does not require an annual public UBO return. The share register (Aktienbuch) must be updated at every ownership transfer; where bearer shares or nominee holdings are used, a beneficiary-owner register must be maintained and disclosed to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration upon request. In practice, the board should verify shareholding and UBO registers before each annual general meeting, and Swiss banks under KYC/CDB rules require periodic UBO confirmation, typically annually, for corporate client accounts.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of shareholders and board meetings
Register of Beneficial Owners where bearer shares or nominee holdings are used

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,000–3,500 per year (approximately CHF 900–3,200) depending on canton and scope of registered office and corporate secretarial services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000–6,000 for a limited review engagement; USD 6,000–25,000 for a full statutory audit by a certified Swiss audit firm

stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
